idiom_name: component interfaces with native interface delegation (by); data-class entities
implementation_notes: Kotlin supports delegation natively - class Entity(private val physics: Physics) : Physics by physics generates every forwarding member with zero boilerplate, which is the language's replacement for the container's hand-written forwarding code - and components are ordinary interfaces plus data classes that own their state, so data class copy/equals/componentN give the entity's shared state value semantics. Use delegated members when the capability set is fixed and a List<Component> only when it changes at runtime, because delegation is bound at construction. A dedicated ECS library (Fleks) is a niche choice in Kotlin, so the idiomatic realization is the general-purpose one.
pitfalls: Delegation with by is fixed at construction: the delegate cannot be swapped for another implementation later, so runtime swappability needs a var holding the component plus explicit forwarding.
Putting a mutable component list in a data class's primary constructor makes equals/hashCode depend on that list, so two logically equal entities compare unequal - keep components in the class body.
Overrides in the delegating class are not seen by the delegate's own code, which can surprise callers expecting full virtual dispatch.
